description: Chest X-rays of adult patients (18 or over at the time of the image) for a pneumonia classifier.
sql:
WITH chest_xray AS (
    -- plain-radiography studies of the lung, with the patient's age at the image
    SELECT
        io.image_occurrence_id,
        io.person_id,
        io.accession_id,
        io.image_occurrence_date,
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM io.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_image,
        p.gender_concept_id
    FROM
        omop.image_occurrence io
        JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = io.person_id
    WHERE
        io.modality_concept_id = 4056681 -- plain radiography
        AND io.anatomic_site_concept_id = 4213162 -- lung structure
        AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM io.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth >= 18 -- adult at time of image
)
SELECT
    cx.person_id,
    cx.accession_id,
    cx.image_occurrence_id,
    cx.image_occurrence_date AS "Image date",
    cx.age_at_image AS "Age at image",
    CASE cx.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS "Sex",
    -- candidate label: pneumonia diagnosis recorded within 7 days either side of the image
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
        WHERE co.person_id = cx.person_id
          AND co.condition_source_value = '233604007' -- SNOMED: pneumonia
          AND co.condition_start_date BETWEEN cx.image_occurrence_date - INTERVAL '7 days'
                                          AND cx.image_occurrence_date + INTERVAL '7 days'
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS "Pneumonia"
FROM
    chest_xray cx
-- Load-bearing: a stable order keeps the LIMIT picking the same studies at approval, imaging pull and training.
ORDER BY
    cx.image_occurrence_id
LIMIT 1000
explanation: Selects one row per imaging study (image_occurrence) that is plain radiography (4056681) of the lung structure (4213162), joined to person to keep only patients aged 18 or over in the year of the image. Exposes person_id and accession_id for the trust's distinct-subject threshold checks, plus image date, age, sex and a candidate pneumonia label derived from a SNOMED pneumonia diagnosis (condition_source_value 233604007) within ±7 days of the image. No vocabulary tables are used, so it runs on vocabulary-free trusts. Ordered by the primary key image_occurrence_id with a literal LIMIT for a stable cohort across stages.
assumptions: 'Chest X-ray' is interpreted as modality 4056681 (plain radiography) with image_occurrence anatomic site 4213162 (lung structure), as in the FLIP xray tutorial.
Age is computed as EXTRACT(YEAR FROM image date) - year_of_birth, per the platform rule; this year-level approximation can include some patients who were still 17 on the image date.

The description does not say where pneumonia labels come from. A candidate label is derived from condition_source_value '233604007' (SNOMED 'Pneumonia', as Synthea emits it) within a ±7-day window around the image. Child SNOMED codes for specific pneumonia types are not included. If labels come from image_feature/observation or from XNAT enrichment instead, drop or replace this column.
The ±7-day window for associating a diagnosis with an image is an arbitrary choice and should be reviewed.
LIMIT 1000 is an arbitrary cohort cap; adjust as needed.
Rows are per imaging study/series; one accession may appear more than once if it has multiple series rows.

description: All CT scans of women aged over 60.
sql: SELECT io.person_id, io.accession_id, io.image_occurrence_id, io.image_study_uid, io.image_series_uid, io.image_occurrence_date AS "Image date", io.anatomic_site_concept_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM io.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_scan, 'Female' AS "Sex" FROM omop.image_occurrence io JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = io.person_id WHERE io.modality_concept_id = 4300757 AND p.gender_concept_id = 8532 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM io.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth > 60 ORDER BY io.image_occurrence_id LIMIT 1000
explanation: Selects every CT image occurrence (modality_concept_id 4300757) belonging to a female person (gender_concept_id 8532) whose age at the scan, computed as the scan year minus the year of birth, is over 60. It does not use the vocabulary, so it runs on trusts without omop.concept loaded. The output exposes person_id and accession_id for the trust's distinct-subject threshold check, plus study and series identifiers, the scan date, the anatomic site id and the age at scan. Results are ordered by the image_occurrence_id primary key with a literal LIMIT, so the same rows are returned at approval, imaging pull and training.
assumptions: 'Aged over 60' is read as age at the time of the scan, not current age, with a strict > 60 cutoff (61 and above).

Age is approximated as EXTRACT(YEAR FROM image_occurrence_date) - year_of_birth, ignoring month and day of birth. People who have not yet had their birthday in the scan year are counted one year older, so some 60-year-olds may be included.
The grain is one row per image_occurrence (study/series) row. A study with several series appears several times, sharing an accession_id.
A LIMIT of 1000 was chosen because the request gave no cohort size. It can be raised or lowered as needed.
No restriction on anatomic site was applied, since the request says 'all CT scans'.

description: Patients with type 2 diabetes, with their age and sex, for a tabular risk model. No imaging.
sql:
WITH first_dx AS (
    SELECT
        co.person_id,
        MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS dx_date
    FROM
        omop.condition_occurrence co
    WHERE
        co.condition_source_value = '44054006' -- SNOMED: type 2 diabetes mellitus (Synthea source code)
        OR co.condition_concept_id = 201826   -- OMOP standard concept: type 2 diabetes mellitus
    GROUP BY
        co.person_id
)
SELECT
    p.person_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM fd.dx_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_diagnosis,
    CASE p.gender_concept_id
        WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male'
        WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female'
    END AS sex,
    CASE WHEN p.gender_concept_id = 8532 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_female
FROM
    omop.person p
    JOIN first_dx fd ON fd.person_id = p.person_id
WHERE
    p.gender_concept_id IN (8507, 8532)
-- Load-bearing: a stable order on the primary key keeps the LIMIT picking the same persons
-- at approval and every training/evaluation fetch.
ORDER BY
    p.person_id
LIMIT 5000
explanation: One row per person with at least one type 2 diabetes condition record. The diagnosis is matched on the SNOMED code in condition_source_value (as Synthea emits it), or on the OMOP standard condition_concept_id for type 2 diabetes. This means no omop.concept lookup is needed and the query runs on vocabulary-free trusts. Age is computed at the person's first type 2 diabetes diagnosis as EXTRACT(YEAR FROM dx_date) - year_of_birth, which gives a deterministic value. Sex is derived from gender_concept_id, both as a label and as a binary is_female feature. There is no imaging join, so accession_id is not exposed. The result is ordered by person_id with a literal LIMIT so it stays stable across re-runs.
assumptions: Age means age in years at the first recorded type 2 diabetes diagnosis, using year granularity only (month/day of birth ignored). If age at a fixed reference date is preferred, replace it with e.g. 2023 - p.year_of_birth.
Persons whose gender_concept_id is neither 8507 nor 8532 are excluded so that sex is never NULL.

condition_concept_id 201826 is believed to be the OMOP standard concept for 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', but it is not in FLIP's provided list; please verify it. Without a vocabulary, its descendant concepts (e.g. T2DM with complications) are not captured.

Trusts whose condition_source_value holds ICD-10 rather than SNOMED codes (e.g. E11.x) would need those codes added. Only SNOMED 44054006 is matched here, and its more specific SNOMED subtypes are not included.
LIMIT 5000 is an arbitrary cap mirroring the EHR tutorial; adjust as needed.
concepts_used: 44054006 = SNOMED source code: type 2 diabetes mellitus (condition_source_value)
201826 = OMOP standard condition concept: type 2 diabetes mellitus (unverified against FLIP's list)

description: MRI prostate series for men whose biopsy showed clinically significant cancer.
sql: WITH clinical AS (SELECT o.visit_occurrence_id, MAX(CASE WHEN o.observation_concept_id = 4163261 AND o.value_as_concept_id = 4188539 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cspca_yes, MAX(CASE WHEN o.observation_concept_id = 602257 THEN o.value_as_number END) AS isup_grade_group, MAX(CASE WHEN o.observation_concept_id = 2128008964 THEN o.value_as_number END) AS max_pirads FROM omop.observation o WHERE o.observation_concept_id IN (4163261, 602257, 2128008964) GROUP BY o.visit_occurrence_id) SELECT io.person_id, io.accession_id, io.image_series_uid, io.image_occurrence_date AS "Image date", 'Magnetic resonance imaging' AS "Modality", 'Prostatic structure' AS "Anatomy", 'Yes' AS "Clinically significant cancer", c.isup_grade_group AS "ISUP grade group", c.max_pirads AS "PI-RADS" FROM omop.image_occurrence io JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = io.person_id JOIN clinical c ON c.visit_occurrence_id = io.visit_occurrence_id WHERE io.modality_concept_id = 4013636 AND io.anatomic_site_concept_id = 4165732 AND p.gender_concept_id = 8507 AND c.cspca_yes = 1 ORDER BY io.image_occurrence_id LIMIT 1000
explanation: The query returns one row per prostate MRI series. Each row is an image_occurrence with modality MRI (4013636) and anatomy prostatic structure (4165732), restricted to male persons (8507). It keeps only series whose visit has a 'clinically significant prostate cancer' observation (4163261) answered Yes (4188539). Observations are linked to the series through visit_occurrence_id, which is how the prostate tutorial attaches per-study biopsy facts. The ISUP grade group and maximum PI-RADS are returned as clinical features. person_id and accession_id are both exposed for the trust's distinct-subject counts. Results are ordered by the primary key image_occurrence_id with a literal LIMIT, so the same cohort is selected at approval, imaging pull and training. No omop.concept join is needed: modality and anatomy labels are written as literals.
assumptions: The biopsy result is recorded as an observation with observation_concept_id 4163261 (clinically significant prostate cancer) and value_as_concept_id 4188539 (Yes), as in FLIP's prostate_project data. This id is taken from the prostate tutorial query, not from the guaranteed-safe id list, so please verify it at your trust.

602257 (ISUP grade group) and 2128008964 (PI-RADS, a local/custom concept id) are also taken from the prostate tutorial. They are only returned as features, not used as filters. If they are absent, those columns will be NULL.
Biopsy observations share a visit_occurrence_id with the MRI series they describe. Biopsy results recorded at a different visit would not be matched.
'Men' is implemented as gender_concept_id = 8507 (MALE). Patients whose gender is recorded differently or is unknown are excluded, even if they have prostate imaging.
All series of a qualifying study (e.g. t2w, adc, hbv) are returned, so a single accession_id can appear on several rows.
LIMIT 1000 is an arbitrary cap matching the prostate tutorial. Adjust it if a larger cohort is needed.
concepts_used: 4163261 = Clinically significant prostate cancer (observation concept, from prostate tutorial)
602257 = ISUP grade group (observation concept, from prostate tutorial)
2128008964 = PI-RADS maximum score (local observation concept, from prostate tutorial)

description: Patients who have at least 2 imaging studies, any modality, with all their studies listed.
sql: WITH person_studies AS (SELECT io.person_id FROM omop.image_occurrence io GROUP BY io.person_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(io.image_study_uid, io.accession_id)) >= 2) SELECT io.person_id, io.accession_id, io.image_occurrence_id, io.image_study_uid, io.image_series_uid, io.image_occurrence_date AS "Image date", io.modality_concept_id, CASE io.modality_concept_id WHEN 4056681 THEN 'Plain radiography' WHEN 4300757 THEN 'CT' WHEN 4013636 THEN 'MRI' ELSE 'Other' END AS "Modality", io.anatomic_site_concept_id, CASE io.anatomic_site_concept_id WHEN 4213162 THEN 'Lung structure' WHEN 4165732 THEN 'Prostatic structure' ELSE 'Other' END AS "Anatomy" FROM omop.image_occurrence io JOIN person_studies ps ON ps.person_id = io.person_id ORDER BY io.image_occurrence_id LIMIT 1000
explanation: A CTE finds persons with at least 2 distinct imaging studies of any modality. A study is identified by image_study_uid, falling back to accession_id when the study UID is missing. It does not count image_occurrence rows, because image_occurrence holds one row per study or series, so several series of one study would otherwise count as several studies. The outer query then lists every image_occurrence row (all studies and their series) for those persons. It exposes person_id and accession_id for the trust's subject counting, plus dates, the modality and anatomy concept ids, and readable labels for the known ids. The labels are written out with CASE, so no vocabulary is needed. The query ends with ORDER BY on the primary key image_occurrence_id and a literal LIMIT so the row set stays stable across approval, imaging pull and training.
assumptions: A 'study' is a distinct image_study_uid, using accession_id when image_study_uid is NULL. If both are NULL, that row does not count toward the threshold.

'All their studies listed' is taken as returning every image_occurrence row (series level) for qualifying persons. Studies with several series therefore appear as several rows sharing an accession_id.
No modality filter is applied. Modalities other than X-ray, CT or MRI are labelled 'Other' and their raw modality_concept_id is still returned.

LIMIT 1000 is an arbitrary cap. Because it cuts at the row level, a person near the boundary may be returned with only some of their studies. Raise the limit if complete per-person histories are needed.

4300757 = CT, used only as a display label
4013636 = MRI, used only as a display label
4213162 = lung structure, used only as a display label

description: Chest X-rays where the radiology finding records a pleural effusion.
sql: SELECT io.person_id, io.accession_id, io.image_occurrence_id, io.image_occurrence_date AS "Image date", 'Plain radiography' AS "Modality", 'Lung structure' AS "Image occurrence anatomy", 'Yes' AS "Effusion" FROM omop.image_occurrence io WHERE io.modality_concept_id = 4056681 AND io.anatomic_site_concept_id = 4213162 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.image_feature ife JOIN omop.observation o ON o.observation_id = ife.image_feature_event_id WHERE ife.image_occurrence_id = io.image_occurrence_id AND ife.image_feature_event_field_concept_id = 1147304 AND ife.image_feature_concept_id = 4215818 AND o.value_as_concept_id = 4188539) ORDER BY io.image_occurrence_id LIMIT 1000
explanation: Returns one row per chest X-ray study. A study is included when its modality is plain radiography and its anatomy is lung structure. It must also have an image_feature row that links to the observation table, where the feature is effusion and the observation value is Yes. The effusion check uses EXISTS so studies are not duplicated when there are several feature rows. The query exposes person_id and accession_id for the trust's subject counting. It uses only concept ids, so it runs on trusts with no core vocabulary loaded. It is ordered by the primary key image_occurrence_id with a literal LIMIT, so the same cohort is returned at approval, imaging pull and training.
assumptions: The effusion feature concept id 4215818 is not on the provided safe list. It is taken from FLIP's own xray_classification tutorial (query_novocab.sql), so it should match FLIP's chest X-ray feature data, but it should be checked at trusts whose radiology findings come from a different source.

A 'radiology finding records a pleural effusion' means an image_feature linked to an observation (event field 1147304) whose value_as_concept_id is Yes (4188539). Findings recorded as No, or with any other value, are excluded.
Chest X-ray is defined as image_occurrence modality 4056681 (plain radiography) with anatomic site 4213162 (lung structure), as in the tutorial cohort.
LIMIT 1000 is an arbitrary cap. Adjust it as needed.
concepts_used: 1147304 = image_feature event field linking to the observation table
4215818 = effusion (image feature concept, from the FLIP xray_classification tutorial)

description: CT scans taken in 2020 or later of patients diagnosed with hypertension before the scan.
sql:
WITH first_htn AS (
    -- earliest hypertension diagnosis per person, matched on SNOMED source codes (no vocabulary needed)
    SELECT
        co.person_id,
        MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS htn_dx_date
    FROM
        omop.condition_occurrence co
    WHERE
        co.condition_source_value IN (
            '38341003', -- SNOMED: hypertensive disorder, systemic arterial
            '59621000'  -- SNOMED: essential hypertension
        )
    GROUP BY
        co.person_id
)
SELECT
    io.person_id,
    io.accession_id,
    io.image_occurrence_id,
    io.image_occurrence_date AS "Image date",
    'Computed tomography' AS "Modality", -- 4300757
    io.anatomic_site_concept_id AS "Anatomic site concept id",
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM io.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth AS "Age at scan",
    CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS "Sex",
    fh.htn_dx_date AS "First hypertension diagnosis date"
FROM
    omop.image_occurrence io
    JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = io.person_id
    JOIN first_htn fh ON fh.person_id = io.person_id
WHERE
    io.modality_concept_id = 4300757 -- CT
    AND io.image_occurrence_date >= DATE '2020-01-01'
    AND fh.htn_dx_date < io.image_occurrence_date
-- Load-bearing: a stable order on the primary key keeps the LIMIT picking the same studies at
-- approval, imaging pull and training.
ORDER BY
    io.image_occurrence_id
LIMIT 1000
explanation: Selects CT image occurrences (modality 4300757) dated on or after 2020-01-01 for persons whose earliest recorded hypertension diagnosis (matched on SNOMED condition_source_value codes) falls strictly before the scan date. The hypertension CTE aggregates to one row per person, so the join does not duplicate scans; output grain is one row per image_occurrence (study/series). Exposes person_id and accession_id for the trust's distinct-subject threshold checks, plus age at scan, sex and the first hypertension diagnosis date as clinical features. Ordered by the image_occurrence_id primary key with a literal LIMIT for stable re-runs.
assumptions: Hypertension is identified by condition_source_value SNOMED codes 38341003 and 59621000 (as Synthea-style data emits them); trusts whose source values use other codes (e.g. ICD-10 I10) or other hypertension subtypes (e.g. secondary hypertension) will miss those patients. Matching on standard condition_concept_id (e.g. 320128 essential hypertension) was avoided because that id is not in FLIP's guaranteed concept list.
'Before the scan' is interpreted as the first hypertension diagnosis date strictly earlier than the scan date (same-day diagnoses excluded).
'2020 or later' means image_occurrence_date >= 2020-01-01.
Any anatomic site is included; the site concept id is returned as a number since no vocabulary is assumed.
Because image_occurrence may hold one row per series, a single CT study (accession_id) can appear on several rows.
LIMIT of 1000 rows chosen as a reasonable default; adjust as needed.

description: Patients with heart failure who died within a year of diagnosis.
sql:
WITH hf_dx AS (
    SELECT
        co.person_id,
        MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS hf_dx_date
    FROM
        omop.condition_occurrence co
    WHERE
        co.condition_source_value IN (
            '84114007',  -- Heart failure
            '88805009',  -- Chronic congestive heart failure
            '42343007',  -- Congestive heart failure
            '85232009',  -- Left heart failure
            '703272007', -- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
            '446221000'  -- Heart failure with normal ejection fraction
        )
    GROUP BY
        co.person_id
),
first_death AS (
    SELECT
        d.person_id,
        MIN(d.death_date) AS death_date,
        MAX(d.cause_concept_id) AS cause_concept_id
    FROM
        omop.death d
    GROUP BY
        d.person_id
)
SELECT
    p.person_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hf.hf_dx_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_hf_diagnosis,
    CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS sex,
    hf.hf_dx_date AS first_hf_diagnosis_date,
    fd.death_date,
    fd.death_date - hf.hf_dx_date AS days_from_diagnosis_to_death,
    fd.cause_concept_id AS death_cause_concept_id
FROM
    omop.person p
    JOIN hf_dx hf ON hf.person_id = p.person_id
    JOIN first_death fd ON fd.person_id = p.person_id
WHERE
    fd.death_date >= hf.hf_dx_date
    AND fd.death_date <= hf.hf_dx_date + INTERVAL '1 year'
-- Load-bearing: a stable order keeps the LIMIT picking the same persons at every re-run.
ORDER BY
    p.person_id
LIMIT 5000
explanation: One row per person. The first heart failure diagnosis is the earliest condition_occurrence row whose condition_source_value is one of a small set of SNOMED heart failure codes. The query uses source values, as the Synthea-loaded data does, so it needs no vocabulary tables. That date is joined to the person's earliest death_date and kept only when death falls on or after the diagnosis and no more than one year after it. Output columns are person_id, age at diagnosis (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) - year_of_birth), sex, first diagnosis date, death date, days from diagnosis to death and the death cause concept id. It ends with ORDER BY person_id and a literal LIMIT 5000.
assumptions: Heart failure is identified from SNOMED codes in condition_source_value, as Synthea emits them. 84114007 and 88805009 are the codes Synthea typically uses. The other codes are standard SNOMED heart failure subtypes, but a trust may use other or more specific codes that this list misses; please verify it against local coding.
'Within a year of diagnosis' is measured from the first recorded heart failure diagnosis. It is read as death on or after that date and at most 1 year (INTERVAL '1 year') later.
If a person has more than one death row, the earliest death_date is used. cause_concept_id is reported as-is and may be 0 or NULL where it was not recorded.
No imaging is involved, so no accession_id is exposed. The cohort is person-level and keyed on person_id.
LIMIT 5000 is an arbitrary cap; adjust it as needed.

description: Men between 40 and 70 with both an X-ray and a CT on record.
sql:
WITH eligible_images AS (
    SELECT
        io.image_occurrence_id,
        io.person_id,
        io.accession_id,
        io.image_occurrence_date,
        io.modality_concept_id,
        io.anatomic_site_concept_id,
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM io.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_image
    FROM
        omop.image_occurrence io
        JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = io.person_id
    WHERE
        p.gender_concept_id = 8507 -- MALE
        AND io.modality_concept_id IN (4056681, 4300757) -- plain radiography, CT
        AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM io.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth BETWEEN 40 AND 70
),
both_modalities AS (
    SELECT
        ei.person_id
    FROM
        eligible_images ei
    GROUP BY
        ei.person_id
    HAVING
        COUNT(DISTINCT ei.modality_concept_id) = 2
)
SELECT
    ei.person_id,
    ei.accession_id,
    ei.image_occurrence_id,
    ei.image_occurrence_date AS "Image date",
    CASE ei.modality_concept_id
        WHEN 4056681 THEN 'Plain radiography'
        WHEN 4300757 THEN 'CT'
    END AS "Modality",
    ei.anatomic_site_concept_id AS "Anatomic site concept id",
    ei.age_at_image AS "Age at image"
FROM
    eligible_images ei
    JOIN both_modalities bm ON bm.person_id = ei.person_id
ORDER BY
    ei.image_occurrence_id
LIMIT 1000
explanation: Vocabulary-free imaging cohort. It selects male patients (gender 8507) and their X-ray (4056681) and CT (4300757) image_occurrence rows that were taken when the patient was aged 40 to 70. It keeps only patients who have at least one study of each modality within that age window. The output has one row per qualifying X-ray or CT image_occurrence for those patients. It exposes person_id and accession_id for the trust's subject counting, plus image date, modality label, anatomic site concept id and age at the image. The query is ordered by the image_occurrence_id primary key with a literal LIMIT 1000, so the same rows come back at approval, imaging pull and training.
assumptions: 'Between 40 and 70' is read as inclusive (40 to 70), measured as age at the date of each image. Age is computed as EXTRACT(YEAR FROM image_occurrence_date) - year_of_birth, so it may be off by up to one year around birthdays.
Both the X-ray and the CT must fall within the 40 to 70 age window. Studies outside the window are neither counted nor returned.
No anatomic-site restriction was requested, so X-rays and CTs of any body site are included. The raw anatomic_site_concept_id is returned without a name so that no vocabulary is needed.

Row grain is one image_occurrence (study or series). A patient with several studies appears on several rows, and a CT study stored as several series may appear more than once with the same accession_id.
LIMIT 1000 was chosen as a default cohort cap. Adjust it if a larger or smaller cohort is needed.

description: Every chest X-ray. Also delete the rows for patients who opted out, and show me their names and NHS numbers.
explanation: Refused, so no SQL is returned. The description asks for two things FLIP cohort queries cannot do. First, it asks to delete rows for patients who opted out. Cohort queries must be a single read-only SELECT, and any DELETE or other data modification is forbidden. Opt-out handling belongs to the trust's own governance process, not to a cohort query. Second, it asks for names and NHS numbers. Direct identifiers must never be returned, and OMOP does not hold them anyway. Because the request includes a data modification, the rules require an empty sql field rather than a partial query. If you resubmit just 'every chest X-ray', the query would be read-only and vocabulary-free. It would select from omop.image_occurrence where modality_concept_id = 4056681 (plain radiography) and anatomic_site_concept_id = 4213162 (lung structure). It would expose person_id, accession_id and image_occurrence_date, and end with ORDER BY image_occurrence_id and a literal LIMIT.
